errors.evidence: The description refers to the figure as a single graph ("Графиката") when it clearly consists of three separate subplots, each illustrating a different correlation value.
The description states the x-axis has intervals of 100, but the tick marks on all three plots are at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1000, indicating intervals of 200.

errors.text_span: Осата Y е означена с числа, започващи от 0 и достигащи до 50, с интервали от 10.
errors.evidence: This description of the Y-axis is only accurate for the middle subplot (rho = 0.5). The other two subplots have entirely different Y-axis ranges and scales, which the description ignores.

errors.text_span: Основната линия, показана в синьо, представлява връх на корелация на 0,25.
errors.evidence: This is a fundamental misinterpretation. The blue line represents one of the two Brownian motion processes, not a correlation value. The value 'rho = 0.25' is a parameter for the entire first subplot, not a property of the blue line itself.

errors.text_span: Линията започва на около 40, достига до максимум на около 400 на Osата X и след това намалява до около 10 края на Osата X.
errors.evidence: This description of the blue line's path is incorrect. It appears to be attempting to describe the middle plot (rho=0.5), but even there, the blue line starts near 0 (not 40) and ends near 30 (not 10).

errors.text_span: Втората линия е показана в оранжево и представлява връх на корелация на 0,50.
errors.evidence: Similar to the error with the blue line, the orange line represents the second Brownian motion process. 'rho = 0.50' is the correlation parameter for the middle subplot, not a property represented by the orange line.
The description claims the orange line starts at a Y-value of approximately 10. In the middle plot (rho=0.5), which this part of the description seems to be about, the orange line starts near 0.

The description fails to explain the main point of the figure, which is to demonstrate how the behavior of two Brownian motions changes as their correlation coefficient (rho) increases across the three plots.
The description completely ignores the existence of the first (rho=0.25) and third (rho=0.75) subplots, focusing only on the middle one (and describing it inaccurately).
